channel.title: The New Yorker — Reporting
channel.description: Latest reporting from The New Yorker

item.title: Have Conservatives Taken Sexy Back?
item.description: The culture wars have come for lingerie as the right, once the advocates of promise rings and purity culture, embarks on a crusade to “Make America Hot Again.”

item.title: Tom Sachs Channels Chanel
item.description: At his downtown studio, the perennially provocative artist makes a lo-fi version of the brand’s flagship Parisian store.

item.title: The Incredible Journey of a Migratory Shorebird
item.description: Godwits make the longest non-stop migration in the bird world. That might be the least of their marvels. Can they survive a changing planet?

item.title: She Made Me Do It
item.description: A prominent dressage trainer shot a belligerent student—and now maintains that he’s the real victim.

item.title: The American Religion of Self-Storage Facilities
item.description: Why are we so obsessed with putting our belongings in metal boxes and then never looking at them again?

item.title: Jared Kushner’s Dollar Diplomacy
item.description: Donald Trump’s son-in-law represents the kind of Washington figure for whom public office serves as a means to extraordinary wealth.

item.title: Israel’s Qatargate Scandal
item.description: Did Benjamin Netanyahu’s aides peddle influence to a foreign power?

item.title: What Barbara Kingsolver Believes the Novel Can Do
item.description: One of the country’s most popular novelists writes what she calls socially engaged fiction. In her new book, she considers the role of art—and who it’s for.

item.title: The Fallout of a Charlie Kirk Campus Scandal
item.description: Students and faculty across the country were punished for their reactions to the conservative activist’s murder. A recent graduate of Texas Tech’s law school is still trying to clear her name.

item.title: Is A.I. Above the Law?
item.description: Our legal system isn’t ready for machines that act on their own.
